input.title: UCL Computer Science MSc personal statement
input.body:
I am applying to the UCL Computer Science MSc to develop my foundations in computer science and prepare for applied research in machine learning. My background is in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, where I developed mathematical, analytical, and computational skills that I now use in machine-learning engineering.

I completed a Bachelor of Engineering in Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Covenant University. My degree work was completed on 28 July 2023 and the degree was awarded on 18 August 2023, with a cumulative GPA of 3.72/4.00. Relevant study included Signals and Systems, Probability and Statistics, Linear Algebra, Control Systems, and Digital Signal Processing. Although my transcript does not include a course titled Machine Learning, these subjects gave me experience with mathematical modelling, signals, statistical reasoning, and analytical problem solving.

Since 8 January 2024 I have worked as a machine-learning engineer at GridSense Africa. I have built load-forecasting pipelines and anomaly-detection prototypes for distribution networks. My technical experience includes Python, PyTorch, embedded C, signal processing, and MLOps. My final-year project concerned edge inference for low-cost power-quality sensors, which strengthened my interest in deploying machine-learning methods under practical hardware and data constraints.

My current research interest is applied machine learning for power-system monitoring, particularly self-supervised event detection and edge inference. A manuscript entitled “Self-supervised event detection for weak distribution grids” was submitted to IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid on 4 May 2026; no decision has been received. This submission reflects my interest in taking engineering problems into more systematic computational and research settings.

The MSc would help me consolidate my computer-science foundations, strengthen my programming and computational-thinking skills, and develop the breadth needed to pursue applied machine-learning research. I am particularly motivated by the opportunity to connect rigorous computer-science study with my experience in signal processing, embedded systems, and energy networks. UCL is an appropriate environment for this transition because the programme accepts strong applicants from engineering backgrounds and emphasises mathematical, analytical, and programming preparation.

I intend to self-fund tuition up to £18,000 and would need financial support for costs above that amount. I have no disciplinary history. I would bring to the programme an engineering perspective, professional experience building machine-learning prototypes, and a clear interest in reliable computational methods for real-world infrastructure.
